chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
The son of the son stands in the place of his father.
ai.seo_question: How does a grandson inherit in Shia law when his father's share?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'representation' (qiwam) in Shia inheritance law, where a grandson stands in the exact place of his deceased father, inheriting the share that father would have received had he been alive. This ruling is foundational to the Shia method of calculating shares, distinguishing it from Sunni schools by ensuring the lineage branch receives its full entitlement without reduction due to the presence of other relatives. The narration underscores the continuity of familial rights through direct male descent, a key tenet in the jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Sukeyn, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A son of the son would stand in the place of his father’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn Sukayn from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Grandchildren take the place of their father.’”
